cands.bio: Republican U.S. representative for North Carolina's 10th District since January 2025. West Point graduate (nuclear engineering, 2009) and former Army Special Forces officer who served in Afghanistan. Co-owner of firearms-industry companies including ZRODelta, UnBrandedAR and US Optics. Lost the 2022 NC-14 race.

endorsements.text: President Donald Trump (R) endorsed Harrigan in the 2026 race, per Ballotpedia.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Harrigan grew up or when he moved to North Carolina. The pages we read do not show any stated position or action from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land conservation, school choice or teacher pay, or foreign-linked donations. We found no stated position or action on pregnancy centers or abortion restrictions beyond a general statement on his website. We also found no documented controversies or foreign ties in the pages available. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2024 or 2026 candidate surveys.

money.note: Individuals gave $118,694; PAC money $7,950; candidate's own money $17,048. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Physician associate with about 15 years in emergency, primary care, rural and telemedicine practice in North Carolina. University educator who teaches evidence-based medicine and research, and a former junior high and high school band director in Texas. Has not held elective office. 2026 Democratic nominee in NC-10.

endorsements.text: Michael Fanone, former DC police officer, listed as an endorser in her Ballotpedia survey and on her campaign site.
Her campaign site lists National Organization for Women, National Women's Political Caucus, Equality NC, Moms Demand Action, NASW-PACE and The Fire PAC among its endorsers and supporters.
Ballotpedia lists Citizens Against AIPAC Corruption among her endorsements and voter guide recommendations.

cands.gaps: We could not establish the year Ashley Bell moved to North Carolina. We found no record of elected or governing office, so there are no actions in office to report. Her campaign lists "Regulate AI and Data Centers" as a top issue, but the text of that plank was not available, so we could not report whether she backs a ban, a moratorium or lighter regulation. We found no documented position on homestead property taxes, growth and land conservation, police pay or pensions, or H-1B visas. Her stated gun position is general ("common sense gun reform") with no specific measures named. We found no news reporting of controversies about her.
